name: hdf5-browser
description: Browse HDF5 (.h5) files in VS Code with kvotab.se's HDF5 Browser: explore the tree, inspect datasets, chart them and export to Excel.
author: Kvot AB

virtualWorkspaces.description: On a virtual file system a file is read whole, up to 1 GB; only a file on disk can be read a piece at a time.

enumDescriptions: Files of 256 MB or more are read a piece at a time, as they are looked at; smaller ones are read whole.
Every file on disk is read a piece at a time.
Every file is read whole, up to 1 GB.
hdf5Browser.readLazily.markdownDescription: How a file is read. Read whole, it is held in the editor's memory; read lazily, the extension's HDF5 reader reads only what is looked at, so a file of any size opens at once. The same rule the [HDF5 Browser](https://kvotab.se/rb.html) applies on the web.

hdf5Browser.addToOpenBrowser.markdownDescription: A file dropped on an HDF5 Browser goes into it as another file tab, as *Add Files* would add it, instead of opening a browser of its own. VS Code opens a dropped file as an editor in the group it was dropped on, so this takes any HDF5 file opened there while a browser shows in the group: a double-click in the Explorer too. A preview (a single click) and *Open Together* still open their own browser, and so does a drop on the edge of a group, which VS Code opens beside it.

enumDescriptions: Light, whatever VS Code is in.
Dark, whatever VS Code is in.
hdf5Browser.theme.markdownDescription: Light or dark mode in the HDF5 Browser's views. The toggle at the right of a view's header sets this; toggling back to the mode VS Code is in sets it to `auto` again.

enumDescriptions: A new version is installed when it is out, and the window is offered a reload to start it.
A new version is offered, and installed if you choose to.
No looking by itself: only HDF5 Browser: Check for Updates looks.
hdf5Browser.updates.markdownDescription: What a new version of the HDF5 Browser leads to. The extension comes from [kvotab.se](https://kvotab.se/rb.html), not from the Marketplace, so it looks there itself, reading the site's release note twice a day: soon after VS Code starts, unless it looked in the last twelve hours, and every twelve hours while VS Code runs. A version is installed only if its signature shows kvotab released it. With VS Code's own `#extensions.autoUpdate#` off, a new version is offered rather than installed; with `#extensions.autoCheckUpdates#` off, the extension looks only when asked, as with `off`.

scripts.test: node build.mjs && python3 test/test-reader.py && python3 test/test-vscode.py
